Say where the blank rows go

Source: R/table_plan.R
plan_blanks.Rd

plan_blanks() places the blank separator rows: between the row groups, after each record of a listing, at the top or bottom of every page, or at positions given. They are added after the page split, so by default they do not count toward a row budget (plan_paginate_rows()); counted = TRUE makes the budget mean the rows the page prints. The rows are kept as positions on each page (pages[[1]]$blank_rows) and appear when the page is rendered.

Usage

plan_blanks(.plan, where = NULL, first = NULL, last = NULL, counted = NULL)

Arguments

.plan

A table_plan().

where

Where blank rows go in the body, as_rtftables(blank_rows = ):

"between_groups"

at every change of group, as plan_row_group() finds it.

"records"

after each record of a listing (listing_spec(blank_row = TRUE)).

"none"

none: a listing's records follow each other with no blank row between them (blank_row = FALSE).

positions

an integer vector, a blank row after each given row; 0 before the first, -1 after the last.

a rule

a blank_rows_by_change() or blank_rows_by_rule() object, or a list() combining any of these.

first, last

TRUE adds one blank row at the top (first) or the bottom (last) of every page, as_rtftables()'s blank_row_first / blank_row_end. On a listing first = FALSE takes away the one the multiline type puts at the top of each page.

counted

TRUE counts the blank rows toward max_rows, as_rtftables(count_blank_rows = ); FALSE (default) does not, so a printed page can be taller than max_rows.

Value

The plan, with one more layer.

See also

plan_verbs for every verb.

Other plan verbs: plan_after(), plan_append(), plan_cell_style(), plan_cells(), plan_col_header(), plan_columns(), plan_compare(), plan_digits(), plan_empty(), plan_filter(), plan_footnotes(), plan_hide(), plan_labels(), plan_levels(), plan_listing(), plan_nest(), plan_paginate_cols(), plan_paginate_group(), plan_paginate_rows(), plan_row_group(), plan_sort(), plan_stat_groups(), plan_stub(), plan_style(), plan_titles(), plan_total()

Examples

st <- data.frame(
  ARM       = rep(c("Placebo", "Active"), each = 3),
  variable  = rep(c("AGE", "SEX", "SEX"), 2),
  .label    = rep(c(NA, "F", "M"), 2),
  .kind     = rep(c("continuous", "categorical", "categorical"), 2),
  stat_name = rep(c("mean", "n", "n"), 2),
  stat      = c(61.2, 12, 8, 63.5, 9, 11))
p <- table_plan(st, cols = "ARM", rows = c(group = "variable")) |>
  plan_cells(continuous = c(Mean = "{mean:.1f}"), categorical = "{n}") |>
  plan_labels(AGE = "Age (years)", SEX = "Sex") |>
  plan_stub(name = "Characteristic")

# Minimal: a blank row between the two blocks (after printed row 2)
pages <- p |> plan_blanks(where = "between_groups") |> plan_apply()
pages[[1]]$blank_rows
#> [1] 2

# The same, with one more at the top and the bottom of the page
pages <- p |>
  plan_blanks(where = "between_groups", first = TRUE, last = TRUE) |>
  plan_apply()
pages[[1]]$blank_rows
#> [1] 0 2 5

# A listing puts one after each record; a compact one puts none
recs <- data.frame(USUBJID = c("01-001", "01-001", "01-002"),
                   AETERM  = c("Headache", "Nausea", "Fatigue"))
table_plan(recs) |>
  plan_listing(listing_col("USUBJID", label = "Subject"),
               listing_col("AETERM", label = "Adverse event")) |>
  plan_blanks(where = "none") |>
  plan_apply()
#> [[1]]
#> ─────────────────────────
#> Subject     Adverse event
#> ─────────────────────────
#> 01-001      Headache     
#> 01-001      Nausea       
#> 01-002      Fatigue      
#> 
#> <rtftable> 3 rows x 3 columns
#>   Columns:    Subject |  | Adverse event
#>   Row title:  col 1
#>   Borders:    set
#>   Widths:     relative 7:1:13
#> 
#>
